programme.title: First Ladies of Hip-Hop
programme.desc: The golden era of hip-hop was dominated by male stars, and its talented women faced a new struggle to make their voices heard as the genre exploded in popularity. With first-hand accounts from leading figures, a look at how women found their voice.

programme.title: Around the World in 80 Gardens
programme.desc: Monty Don visits the world's 80 most inspiring gardens. In Mexico, Monty visits the ancient water gardens of Mexico City and a surrealist fantasy garden hidden in the rainforest. In Cuba, he discovers a green revolution sprouting out of crumbling colonial lawns.

programme.title: BBC Proms
programme.desc: Tom Service curates a special compilation of new music, featuring two world premieres, a dazzling trumpet concerto, cinematic sound-scapes and insightful interviews with composers.

programme.title: Imagine...
programme.sub-title: George Benjamin: What Do You Want To Do When You Grow Up?
programme.desc: He has been crowned with every laurel in contemporary classical music, composed operas which play on the world's most illustrious stages, and been knighted for his services to music. Yet Sir George Benjamin is still relatively little known outside the classical world.

programme.title: Royal Opera House - Lessons in Love and Violence
programme.desc: Sir George Benjamin conducts the world premiere of his darkly dramatic opera based on the life of Edward II, a major event in contemporary music with an internationally renowned cast, this is the latest collaboration between composer George Benjamin and playwright Martin Crimp. Their previous work includes the large-scale opera `Written on Skin', which has since become the most performed new opera of the 21st century.

programme.title: Omnibus
programme.sub-title: Virginia Woolf: A Night's Darkness, A Day's Sail
programme.desc: A film that celebrates the lyricism of Virginia Woolf's writing and, through the memories of her friends and relations, paints a portrait of a dedicated artist and a unique companion. It also tries to show how the contradictions in her character were triumphantly resolved in her art. Among the many people taking part in the film are Elizabeth Bowen, Lord David Cecil, Duncan Grant, Raymond Mortimer, George Rylands and Virginia Woolf's nephew, Professor Quentin Bell.

programme.title: Planet Earth
programme.desc: A look at deserts, which cover a third of the earth's land surface. From space they appear lifeless but a closer inspection reveals a different picture. Deserts are in fact surprisingly varied, from Mongolia's Gobi desert, where wild Bactrian camels have to eat snow in lieu of water, to the Atacama in Chile where guanacos survive by licking the dew off cactus spines.

programme.title: The Latest Secrets of the Hieroglyphs
programme.desc: In 1822, Jean-François Champollion became the first person to decipher hieroglyphs in over a thousand years. Now, a new generation of Egyptologists is learning more about the people who wrote them.

programme.title: I Am Martin Parr
programme.desc: Examines the work of contemporary photographer Martin Parr, known for his unique and intimate approach to his subjects.

programme.title: Modern Times
programme.desc: As another St George's Day passes, Martin Parr, the celebrated Magnum stills photographer, travels the length and breadth of the country to look at the English and how they see themselves.

programme.title: Timeshift
programme.desc: A celebration of the British seaside holiday experience from its Victorian origins and heyday in the 1950s to its slow decline and attempts at reinvention since. Interviewees including Jonathan Meades, Martin Parr and Bill Pertwee explain the way that the seaside has always been the place we all visit to lose our inhibitions and reveal a different side to ourselves.

programme.title: Welsh Greats
programme.desc: The life story of the girl from Dowlais whose flair for design made her a multimillionaire. From printing scarves on the kitchen table to running an international business empire, she never forgot her Welsh roots.

programme.title: Timeshift
programme.sub-title: Bouffants, Beehives and Bobs - The Hairstyles That Shaped Britain
programme.desc: A look at the story of the iconic hairstyles that defined postwar Britain, from the meringue-like confections of Raymond `Teasy Weasy' Bessone, to the `architectural' precision cutting of Vidal Sassoon, via the bouffant, beehive and bob.

programme.title: The Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers
programme.desc: Hobbits Frodo and Sam discover they are being followed by the mysterious Gollum. Middle-earth Aragorn, the Elf archer Legolas and Gimli the Dwarf encounter the besieged Rohan kingdom, whose once great King Theoden has fallen under Saruman's deadly spell.

programme.title: The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King
programme.desc: The final part of the fantasy trilogy based on JRR Tolkien's epic tale. Despite Gollum, hobbits Frodo and Sam reach Mordor in their quest to destroy the `one ring', while Aragorn leads the forces of good against Sauron's evil army at the stone city of Minas Tirith. Then, to buy Frodo and Sam time, they must march to the very gates of Mordor to distract Sauron's gaze from the Ring bearer.
